Hold§9 65,536 SM on an L1 lattice for 1 hour§r, with no leak: the top of the L1 band, and the hole the Eye's T9 → T10 Supermassive Link asks for.

§5§lOVER §lTHE §lLIMIT§r Mass over the safe limit has no time limit: the §9hold-up gas§r holds it. At a band top that is 3× Eddington on top of the disc, so at least§9 4× Eddington§r of intake: 1.31 M L/t of Hydrogen, or 2.62 M of Helium, at 65,536 SM.

§5§lA §lLEAK§r When the hold-up is short (the amber segment shows red), the extra mass leaks back: the part over the safe limit halves each hour on a log scale, never below the safe limit, and nothing is damaged. A dark disc holds nothing, so an outage leaks too; the 60 s Accretion Buffer covers a short one.

§5§lAUTOMATE§r The Directive Hatch's Horizon set: [1] hold-up short, [2] buffer under 30 s, [4] anchor short, [8] Overdrive upkeep short. A Burst Control Hatch in Hold mode sets the setpoint (redstone 1 the safe limit .. 15 the band top; 0 leaves the GUI's setpoint, so an unwired hatch changes nothing). Sensor channels and OpenComputers (getHoldUp, getBuffer) report it.

Holding exactly 65,536 SM leaves no margin: keep the §9Accretion Buffer§r full (60 s), so a short supply gap never leaks the hole under the Supermassive Link's 65,536 SM.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r the hole has held 65,536 SM for an hour with the hold-up fully paid, no leak (tick the box).
